title-group.article-title: Tapinarof cream 1% for corticosteroid-refractory erythema annulare centrifugum: A first reported case

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Erythema annulare centrifugum (EAC) is a reactive annular erythema of uncertain aetiology. Treatment is often unsatisfactory1,2 and relapses are common after topical corticosteroids are withdrawn.

sec.title: Case report
sec.p: A 54-year-old woman presented with a 3-year history of expanding annular plaques on the trunk that had failed clobetasol 0.05% ointment and oral antihistamines. Tapinarof cream 1% was applied once daily. At 4 weeks the plaques had flattened and erythema had reduced by roughly 70%; at 12 weeks the lesions had cleared with residual post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation. No adverse events were reported.

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: Aryl hydrocarbon receptor agonism may modulate the interface dermatitis seen in EAC. This case suggests tapinarof may be an option for corticosteroid-refractory EAC, although controlled data are needed.
